title: Design System: BMW Product Strategy AI

headline.purpose: Every product slide headline; uppercase, ends in a period.

numeral.purpose: Requirement ranks and funnel counts; tabular figures.

statement.purpose: PM quote and voice transcript, light white.

lede.purpose: One-sentence line under each headline, mist.

button.purpose: Uppercase labels on buttons; tiles at 17px/600.

label.purpose: Uppercase field labels, rail steps, status, context chips.

tag.purpose: Evidence, assumption, rejected, AI and gap tags.

motion.name: ease-keynote
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for every transition, entrance, and auto-animate morph.

motion.name: auto-animate
motion.purpose: Slide-to-slide morph of headline, rows, rail progress and head.

motion.name: control-state
motion.purpose: Hover and press on buttons, tiles, row actions.

motion.name: ground-drift
motion.purpose: Slow drift of the keynote ground image.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every animation and transition.

assets.name: keynote-ground
assets.purpose: The only background; navy to petrol to plum keynote image.

assets.name: concept-car
assets.purpose: Keynote AI concept sedan; bleeds into the ground through gradient masks.

narrative.overview:
This system is BMW's own product-management keynote carried forward into software. The ground is the keynote's own atmospheric image (navy into petrol into plum), not a colour we chose, and every surface on it is drawn the way the keynote draws "The Process": white hairline rectangles with square corners, bold condensed uppercase headlines that end in a period, and a light condensed voice for everything that explains. The product content (ranked requirements, evidence, rejections, voice-captured reasons) lives inside that drawing language, so a BMW PM reads it as the next slide of their own deck rather than a vendor dashboard.

Density is a keynote stage, not an app screen: a fixed 1280 by 720 canvas, a 56px gutter, one idea per slide, and a persistent process rail along the bottom that says where in BMW's process the viewer stands. Colour is spent on meaning only. BMW blue is the action and the AI's fresh proposal, M red is rejection and weakness, ice and amber split evidence from assumption. Everything else is white, ice, mist, steel, and slate on the ground.

Authorship is visible everywhere. A robot glyph marks what the AI proposed and a person glyph marks what the PM decided, both drawn from the keynote's own icon set. The system rejects the generic SaaS dark dashboard: no rounded glowing cards, no drop-shadowed panels, no gradient fills on surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: The keynote ground image as the only background; surfaces are hairline outlines on it, never filled cards.
Square corners everywhere except the voice-capture control.
Condensed uppercase display headlines ending in a period; light semi-condensed body.
Colour carries meaning: blue acts, red rejects, ice is evidence, amber is assumption.
Robot and person glyphs mark who authored every item.
A process rail on every product slide, advancing with the story.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Blue means act or newly proposed by the AI, red means rejected or weak, ice means evidence, amber means assumption. No hue appears for decoration.

rules.name: The One Blue Button Rule
rules.body: A slide carries at most one filled BMW blue button. Every other control is a hairline outline.

rules.name: The Ground Is Given Rule
rules.body: The background is the keynote's own image (assets/keynote-ground.webp) over night. Never replace it with a CSS gradient or a flat fill, and never paint surfaces over it with opaque panels.

rules.name: The Keynote Headline Rule
rules.body: Product headlines are condensed, bold, uppercase, set tight (0.95 leading, 0 tracking), and end with a period, like a keynote statement. Headlines never sit under a small label or kicker.

rules.name: The Weight Contrast Rule
rules.body: Explanation is light (300) and decisions are bold (700). Inside a light sentence, the decisive figure is bolded in white ("144 of 157").

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every count and rank uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The No Lift Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows on surfaces, buttons, rows, or images. A surface that needs emphasis changes its tint or its line, not its height.

dos: **Do** set every slide on the keynote ground image (assets/keynote-ground.webp) over night.
**Do** draw surfaces as white hairline rectangles: 1.5px for frames, 1px soft hairline for subdivisions, square corners.
**Do** end product headlines with a period, in Saira Condensed 700 uppercase.
**Do** open every piece of AI reasoning with an Evidence, Assumption, or Evidence gap tag.
**Do** mark authorship with the robot glyph (AI proposes) or the person glyph (PM decides).
**Do** keep the process rail on every product slide and advance it with the story.
**Do** use tabular numerals for every count and rank, and bold the decisive figure in white.
donts: **Don't** round corners on frames, buttons, tiles, tags, or rows; the circle belongs to the voice-capture control alone.
**Don't** add drop shadows or glows to surfaces; emphasise with tint or line weight.
**Don't** place more than one filled BMW blue button on a slide.
**Don't** use M red for anything other than rejection or weakness.
**Don't** fill surfaces with opaque or gradient card backgrounds over the ground; the only solid surface is the white verdict bar.
**Don't** put a small label or kicker above a headline.
**Don't** substitute a CSS gradient for the keynote ground image.
